title: Failure-mode mapping: promptset syndromes and remediation roadmap
content:
Overview:

This is a working diagnostic and remediation roadmap for the recent onboarding regression observed when moving model v2.4 -> v2.5 on our standard prompt coverage suite (promptset 'core-coverage-v1'). The intent of this doc is to map failure modes to concrete prompt archetypes ("syndromes"), propose short/medium/long-term mitigations, and define experiments and rollout controls. This is a working draft — data and hypotheses are provisional.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Symptom: 11% drop in pass@threshold for intent-preservation tests and a 6% increase in hallucination rate on knowledge-verification tasks after model v2.5 onboarding. Latency within SLO.
- Root clusters: three dominant failure-mode clusters: "context truncation misalignment", "instruction-following erosion on edge templates", and "entity hallucination with multi-step chaining".
- Short-term fixes (1–2 weeks): prompt-level hardened templates, canonical fallback instructions, and model routing to v2.4 for top 3 customers with high sensitivity.
- Medium-term (1–2 months): evaluation harness updates (new unit prompts), targeted fine-tuning (instruction reinforcement on archetypes), and safety tokenization checks.
- Long-term (2–6 months): automated prompt-stress testing, trimmed/augmented pretraining data audit for chain-of-thought fragmentation, and integrated regression gating in CI for onboarding.

Scope and impact: 
- Affects: onboarding of open and verified models (v2.5 candidate) for hosted API and Dedicated tiers. Private deployments not impacted for customers who pinned older versions.
- Datasets used: promptset 'core-coverage-v1' (12k prompts; composed of intent-preservation, instruction-clarity, knowledge-lookup, and multi-step reasoning subsets), internal anchored QA (anchor-qa-3k), and synthetic chain prompts (chain-synth-1k).
- Metrics monitored: pass@threshold (binary acceptance by rubric), hallucination-rate (asserted false facts per 1k responses), instruction-drop (measured token deviation from required action), latency p50/p95.

Evaluation summary (key numbers):
- baseline v2.4: pass@threshold 0.93; hallucination-rate 18 / 1k; instruction-drop 2.3%
- candidate v2.5: pass@threshold 0.83; hallucination-rate 24 / 1k; instruction-drop 8.6%
- biggest regressions: intent-preservation subset (-11% absolute), multi-step reasoning (-9% absolute).

Error clustering (observed clusters and examples):
1) Context truncation misalignment
   - Description: model omits or mis-prioritizes earlier instruction fragments when prompts contain non-uniform separators or long metadata blocks. Appears more frequently when prompts include long system notes (> 120 tokens) followed by short user queries.
   - Representative prompts (anonymized): long system preface + "Summarize the three steps" -> output describes two steps and invents 3rd.
   - Frequency: ~28% of failing samples in the instruction-clarity subset.
   - Hypothesis: attention/scoring change in v2.5 reduces positional bias for earlier context when separator tokens are unusual (\"---\" vs \"###\").

2) Instruction-following erosion on edge templates
   - Description: Highly templated instructions (e.g., "Return only a JSON array of objects with keys x,y,z") returned extraneous commentary or skipped fields. Mostly reproducible on terse prompts with strict format constraints.
   - Representative prompts: "Given this list, output JSON array with fields: id,label" -> model responds with natural language intro then JSON, or omits id field.
   - Frequency: ~42% of failing samples in the intent-preservation and format subsets.
   - Hypothesis: calibration shift in v2.5 toward safer, more verbose completions when instruction tokens are low-probability under new logits distribution.

3) Entity hallucination in multi-step chaining
   - Description: In multi-step tasks requiring verification (e.g., multi-hop QA), the model produces plausible but incorrect intermediate facts, then uses them to justify final answers.
   - Representative prompt: "Find the population of town X, then compute per-capita metric" -> model fabricates population and computes.
   - Frequency: ~21% of failing samples in chain-synth subset.
   - Hypothesis: weaker grounding after beam/temperature defaults changed; also may be associated with small shifts in knowledge embedding weights in v2.5.

Other observed anomalies (lower frequency):
- Tokenization boundary changes causing truncated entity names when special unicode appears (<5%).
- Rare mode collapse to template completion on list-generation tasks (<3%).

Prompt archetypes (syndromes) mapped to failure clusters:
- "Long-preface + terse-instruction" -> context truncation misalignment.
- "Strict-formatter" (short instruction + explicit schema) -> instruction-following erosion.
- "Chain-verify" (multi-step with intermediate lookups) -> entity hallucination.
- "Unicode-edge" (names with special punctuation) -> tokenization boundary issues.

Root cause hypotheses (ranked by plausibility):
1) Model internals: subtle changes to positional bias and attention normalization in v2.5 (primary). Evidence: attention-weight inspection on sample fails shows reduced attention mass on earliest context tokens in failing runs.
2) Decoding default changes: temperature/penalty tweaks in the candidate runtime that shipped with onboarding (secondary). Evidence: reproduces locally when decoding matches runtime defaults in CI.
3) Tokenizer updates: small changes to byte-level mapping for specific unicode sequences (tertiary). Evidence: small set of mismatch cases correlate with new token boundaries.

Immediate triage actions (done or in-progress):
- Reverted runtime decoding defaults for the canary fleet -> reduced hallucination-rate by ~30% on canary (JIRA-AML-1023).
- Added prompt-level detection that flags unusual separators and injects canonical separator token (\"###\") when observed (PR: models#789).
- Temporarily pinned high-sensitivity customers to v2.4 with a routing override.

Proposed mitigations and experiments:
Short-term (sprint, 1–2 weeks):
- Hardened templates: add canonical separator insertion in prompt preprocessor for hosted API. Quick win; low risk. Test plan: A/B on 10k sample promptset with and without insertion. Success metric: restore pass@threshold > 0.90.
- Strict-format wrapper: for calls with format_flag=true, prepend explicit enforcement token: "OUTPUT_ONLY_JSON_V1" and strip natural language prefixes in responses (postprocess). Success: reduce extraneous commentary by 80% in intent-preservation subset.
- Routing fallbacks: automated fallback to v2.4 for requests matching prompt archetype signatures (regex + length heuristics). Requires config knob in gateway; immediate rollout to 1% of traffic then ramp.

Medium-term (1–2 months):
- Focused instruction-reinforcement fine-tune on 50k synthetic and curated examples emphasizing strict-format prompts and long-preface/short-instruction combos. Evaluate on holdout core-coverage-v1 splits.
- Update evaluation harness: expand promptset with targeted adversarial variations (separator variants, unicode edge cases, chained verifications with counterfactual distractors).
- Tokenizer audit: run diffs between v2.4 and v2.5 tokenization for all anchor-qa-3k entities; if divergence > 0.5% for entity tokens, roll tokenizer patch or add pre-normalization.

Long-term (2–6 months):
- Integrate regression gating into model onboarding CI: require pass@threshold delta < 2% across key subsets and a hallucination-rate non-increase. Block autopromotion otherwise.
- Data-level audit: probe pretraining/continual-update corpora slices for chain-of-thought truncation artifacts; consider augmenting with verified chains.
- Model-level fixes: if attention positional drift is confirmed, implement patch and re-evaluate; otherwise, bake prompt-engineering strategies into default SDK.

Risk and tradeoffs:
- Prompt preprocessor insertion may mask underlying model issues and induce coupling between customers' prompt style and our preprocessors. Must expose opt-out and document behavior.
- Fine-tuning may reduce general capabilities if not balanced; holdout evaluation and adversarial checks necessary.
- Routing fallbacks increase operational complexity and must respect customer SLAs and transparency.

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Experiment A (preprocessor insertion): sample size 10k, metric: pass@threshold; acceptance: >= 0.90, no latency p95 increase >5%
- Experiment B (format enforcement token): sample size 5k across JSON-formatting prompts; metric: extraneous_phrase_rate; acceptance: <= 5%
- Experiment C (decode defaults revert): small-scale AB on canary fleet; metric: hallucination-rate; acceptance: >20% relative improvement

Rollout plan & gating:
- Week 0: continue canary with decode defaults reverted; run preprocessor insertion A/B on canary-internal traffic.
- Week 1: if A passes, rollout preprocessor to 10% production; enable routing fallback for top 5 customers.
- Week 2–6: run medium-term fine-tuning experiments in parallel; ensure CI gating for v2.5 re-promotion only after meeting thresholds.

Monitoring and observability additions required:
- Add per-archetype counters in Console (route and model level): long-preface, strict-formatter, chain-verify, unicode-edge.
- Add automated alert when pass@threshold drops >3% within a 24h window for any model in production.
- Add example-never-redact logging for failing cases to speed triage (privacy review required).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is the attention drift intentional (experimental change in pretraining architecture) or emergent from training schedule differences? Need model-research input (action: @Luca).
- Could small decoding changes explain the instruction-drop alone? Need controlled decode ablation across many seeds.
- Are there private deployment customers who observed different failure rates due to custom tokenizer settings? Ask solutions-eng to surface.

Action items (owners and target dates):
- Add canonical separator insertion to hosted preprocessor (owner: Samir Patel) — target: 2026-03-08 — JIRA-AML-1030.
- Implement format-enforce wrapper in SDK (owner: Priya Natarajan) — target: 2026-03-12 — PR: sdk#1024.
- Run tokenizer diff audit and produce a short report (owner: Maya Chen) — target: 2026-03-10.
- Start instruction-reinforcement fine-tune job and produce preliminary eval (owner: Luca Martinez) — target: 2026-04-01.
- Update onboarding CI with gating thresholds (owner: eng-release) — target: 2026-04-15.

Appendix A: quick reproduction snippets (for engineers)
- Minimal repro for strict-formatter: POST payload with prompt: "Return only JSON array of objects with keys id,name. Items: [Alice, Bob]". Compare v2.4 vs v2.5 with decode defaults set to {temperature:0.0, top_p:1.0}.
- Minimal repro for long-preface: system: "Context: <200 token legalese>" + user: "List three compliance steps". Check attention map on token positions 1..20.

Appendix B: logs & artifacts locations
- Raw eval runs: gs://redwood-evals/core-coverage-v1/v2.5/2026-02-18/*.ndjson
- Analysis notebook (work in progress): https://colab.research.google.com/drive/1-example-notebook
- Related tickets: JIRA-AML-1023 (decoder revert), JIRA-AML-1030 (preprocessor insertion)

Notes to self / typos to clean up later:
- Need to add confidence intervals to reported metrics.
- Should quantify latency impact of preprocessor more precisely.
- Verify that SDK enforcement token doesn't collide with customer input.

If you are reading this and have run reproductions, drop short notes in the comments or link PRs — I'll consolidate results here.

— Maya
